### **6. Soccer**

#### Rules & How the Game Works
* **Golden‑Goal Overtime** – MPSSAA uses a **golden‑goal** period for tied playoff games; the Star‑Democrat notes the dramatic 2022 *Queen Anne’s* vs. *St. Michael’s* quarterfinal that ended on a 78‑second golden goal.  
* **Substitution Limits** – Up to **five** substitutions per game in regular season; many coaches use **early sub patterns** to manage the **heat** on the open fields of Dorchester.  

#### Key Stats & What They Mean
| Stat | Shore Insight |
|------|----------------|
| **Possession %** | Teams holding **> 55 %** (e.g., *Kent Island* in 2023) are typically the **tournament favorites**. |
| **Shots on Goal** | A high **SOG** count (≥ 15 per game) indicates an aggressive **pressing style** used by *Easton*. |
| **Goal Differential** | A +10 differential by mid‑season is a strong predictor of **playoff seeding**. |

#### What Decides Games on the Eastern Shore
* **Field Surface** – Most schools use **grass** that can become **boggy** after rain, slowing **possession‑based** teams and favoring **counter‑attack** sides.  
* **Travel & Time Zones** – Teams traveling to **Baltimore area** for non‑conference matches (e.g., *Queen Anne’s* vs. *Baltimore County*) face **long bus rides**, often affecting stamina.  
* **Coaching Philosophy** – *Easton* employs a **possession‑centric** 4‑4‑2, while *CSD* favors a **direct 4‑3‑3** with wing‑back overlaps.  

#### Positions & Terminology
| Position | Local Reference |
|----------|-----------------|
| **Center Forward** | “**Goal‑Poacher**” – the player who scores the **late‑game clincher** (e.g., *Mia Hughes* for *Easton*). |
| **Holding Midfielder** | “**Pivot**” – the anchor that breaks up attacks, highlighted in *Kent Island*’s **defensive midfield** unit. |
| **Full‑Back** | “**Wing‑Back**” – used in stories about *CSD*’s overlapping runs that create **crossing opportunities**. |

#### What to Watch For
* **“The Spring Classic”** – An annual tournament hosted by *Queen Anne’s* that brings in **out‑of‑state** teams; the **All‑Tournament Team** is a frequent feature.  
* **“Rain‑Delay Drama”** – A sudden downpour in the **third period** often leads to **field‑condition debates** that dominate post‑game coverage.  
* **“Senior Night Scoring Bouts”** – Seniors often produce **multiple‑goal games**, a hallmark of Star‑Democrat’s “Senior Spotlight” columns.  

#### Interview Tips
* **Coach Tactics** – Ask about **adjustments** when the field turns **muddy** (e.g., “Do you shift to a more direct style?”).  
* **Player Pathways** – Highlight **club‑team experiences**; many Shore players also compete in **Baltimore area clubs**.  
* **Community Angle** – Emphasize the **family atmosphere** at games (parents serving as **concession volunteers**).  

#### Story Angles
| Angle | Sample Headline |
|-------|-----------------|
| **Program Rebuild** | “*Cambridge‑South Dorchester* looks to bounce back after a 3‑year winless stretch, focusing on a new defensive system.” |
| **Breakout Freshman** | “Freshman *Liam Cole* tallies 8 goals, the most by a first‑year player since 2018.” |
| **Rivalry Spotlight** | “*Easton* edges *Kent Island* 2‑1 in a tightly contested Bay‑Bridge soccer clash.” |
| **Coach Milestone** | “*Coach Dan Miller* reaches 150 career wins, the most in Shore soccer history.” |
| **Weather‑Driven Upset** | “A sudden thunderstorm forces a field swap; *CSD* adapts and pulls off a 3‑2 upset over *Queen Anne’s*.” |

### **7. Softball**

#### Rules & How the Game Works
* **Run‑Rule** – MPSSAA applies a **run‑rule after 5 innings** if a team leads by 8+ runs; a 2022 *Princess Anne* 12‑0 mercy‑rule win is a classic example of a **dominant pitching staff**.  
* **Pitch‑Count** – Same 75‑pitch limit as baseball; **freshman pitchers** often hit the cap early in the season, prompting **early‑season rotation experiments**.  

#### Key Stats & What They Mean
| Stat | Shore Context |
|------|----------------|
| **Batting Average (BA)** | A team BA > .300 is considered **offensive powerhouse**; *Kent Island* posted .312 in 2023. |
| **Earned Run Average (ERA)** | An ERA < 2.00 signals a **dominant staff**; *Princess Anne* posted 1.45 in 2022. |
| **Fielding %** | High fielding percentages (> .950) are prized on **grass fields** that can cause **bad hops**. |

#### What Decides Games on the Eastern Shore
* **Field Quality** – Many **grass** diamonds become **uneven** after rain, favoring **contact hitters** over power hitters.  
* **Travel Fatigue** – Teams crossing the **Salisbury Bridge** for **back‑to‑back Thursday–Friday** series often see **late‑inning scoring drops**.  
* **Depth of Pitching** – Because of **pitch‑count rules**, a **deep bullpen** (often built from **junior varsity** players) is a competitive advantage in district tournaments.  

#### Positions & Terminology
| Position | Local Phrase |
|----------|--------------|
| **Pitcher** | “**Ace**” – the staff’s workhorse (e.g., *Senior pitcher *Avery Cole*). |
| **Catcher** | “**Battery Leader**” – the catcher who calls games, often highlighted in **“Catcher’s Corner”** pieces. |
| **Shortstop** | “**Middle‑Infield Maestro**” – a key defensive position on **rough fields**. |
| **Designated Player (DP)** | “**Power Hitter**” – used to describe a **slugger** who rarely fields (e.g., *Mia Hughes* for *Kent Island*). |

#### What to Watch For
* **“The Southern Showdown”** – *Princess Anne* vs. *Mardela* on a Tuesday night draws > 1,200 fans; the **“Southern Crown”** is a coveted title.  
* **“Tournament Traditions”** – The **Bayside Softball Tournament** at *Cambridge‑South Dorchester* includes a **“home‑run derby”** that the Star‑Democrat covers each June.  
* **“Senior Night Heroics”** – Seniors often finish with **multiple hits** or a **shutout**; these are staple **human‑interest** pieces.  

#### Interview Tips
* **Coach Legacy** – Ask veteran coaches (e.g., *Coach Lisa Miller* at *Princess Anne*) about **program evolution** since the 1990s.  
* **Player Family Stories** – Many players are **second‑generation** (e.g., *the Dantzler sisters*); explore **family dynamics**.  
* **Post‑Season Stakes** – Emphasize the **automatic district bid** that the **Bayside champion** secures; it raises the narrative stakes.  

#### Story Angles
| Angle | Example |
|-------|---------|
| **Program Rebuild** | “*Princess Anne* rebuilds after a 4‑year playoff absence, leaning on a deep freshman class.” |
| **Breakout Freshman** | “Freshman *Jenna Cole* posts a .380 BA, the highest for a first‑year player in a decade.” |
| **Coach Milestone** | “*Coach Lisa Miller* records her 500th win, the first in Eastern Shore softball history.” |
| **Rivalry Recap** | “*Princess Anne* clinches the ‘Southern Showdown’ with a 9‑2 victory over *Mardela*.” |
| **Weather‑Driven Story** | “A sudden downpour forces a game postponement; the *Kent Island* staff uses the extra day for a bullpen showcase.” |

### **8. Wrestling**

#### Rules & How the Game Works
* **Bayside Tiebreaker** – In conference dual meets, the **team with the most classification points** wins the tie (used in the 2023 *Easton* vs. *Queen Anne’s* 5‑5 dual).  
* **Overtime Structure** – MPSSAA uses **sudden‑death** overtime; the Star‑Democrat highlights **“last‑second pins”** as dramatic finishers (2022 *CSD* senior *Tyler Miller* pinned in 2 seconds).  

#### Key Stats & What They Mean
| Stat | Shore Meaning |
|------|----------------|
| **Classification Points** | A higher total (e.g., 78 vs. 72) indicates **depth across weight classes**; *CSD* led the conference with 84 points in 2023. |
| **Pins** | Pin counts are a **measure of dominance**; *Queen Anne’s* recorded 23 pins in the 2022 season. |
| **Technical Fall Rate** | A high rate (> 30 %) shows **superior technique**; *Easton* posted 35 % in 2021. |

#### What Decides Games on the Eastern Shore
* **Weight‑Class Depth** – Smaller schools often lack **upper‑weight** depth; success hinges on **mid‑weight** dominance (e.g., *CSD*’s 145‑lb champion).  
* **Travel** – Dual meets often require **hour‑long bus rides** to neighboring counties; fatigue can affect **late‑match performance**.  
* **Coaching Experience** – Long‑tenured coaches (e.g., *Coach Brian Holt* at *Easton*, 18 years) bring **technical refinement** that translates into **higher pin rates**.  

#### Positions & Terminology
| Position | Local Lingo |
|----------|-------------|
| **Freestyle Wrestler** | “**Mat‑Master**” – used for wrestlers who excel in **open‑mat** situations. |
| **Greco‑Roman Specialist** | “**Clincher**” – a wrestler who focuses on **upper‑body throws**; highlighted in **“Throw‑of‑the‑Week”** stories. |
| **Weight‑Class** | Referred to as “**Division**” in some local coverage (e.g., “the 152‑division”). |

#### What to Watch For
* **“Girls’ Wrestling Rise”** – 2024 saw *Queen Anne’s* girls’ team win the **first state title** for the Shore; a historic angle the Star‑Democrat covered extensively.  
* **“Dual Meet Rivalries”** – *Easton* vs. *CSD* is a **classic showdown**; the 2022 dual ended 6‑6 with *Easton* winning on classification points.  
* **“Tournament Traditions”** – The **Bayside Invitational** at *Salisbury High* includes a **“Coach’s Corner”** award for sportsmanship.

* **Coach Philosophy** – Discuss **training philosophies** (e.g., “How do you balance strength vs. technique?”).  
* **Athlete Journey** – Many wrestlers start in **youth clubs**; ask about **transition to high school** and **college aspirations**.  
* **Gender Angles** – With the **girls’ program** gaining momentum, explore **title IX impact** and community support.

NOTES AFTER FACT CHECK: 

I spent about an hour fact checking this document. After about 30 min I realized that there was no reason to continue fact checking because just about everything was wrong. It is a bummer. Some stuff is just slightly off. 75 pitches vs. 95 pitches for the minimum for a 9th grader. Some stuff makes no sense at all. Making up rivalries, making up when teams play, making up that teams share fields, making up rules for the sport, making up the powerhouse programs. Yuck. This is not journalism at all. I don’t know where we went wrong. I searched in the baseball metadata about shared fields and it is not in there. So the LLM legit just made it up. 

I made my beat book by 1. Generating metadata by high school sports. 2. Taking that metadata to create sport specific beat books. 3. Combined all the beat books and used that to make a larger complete beat book. 

I have a lot of places where the LLM could have made stuff up, whether in the first set of sports specific beat books or the second set where I combined them. 

I think I need to take a step back as I was pushing for a lot of content in my beat book. It is 16 pages long. But I would rather give a reporter 2 pages of great true information than 16 pages of bull shit. 

As I remake my beat book one final time I will keep that in mind and fact check as I go! I am going to go back to square one and make metadata again for all these articles and hope to keep the BS from seeping into the beat book.

```python
import json
import re

def clean_key(key):
    # Lowercase, replace spaces and hyphens with underscores, remove duplicate underscores
    key = key.lower().replace(" ", "_").replace("-", "_")
    key = re.sub(r'_+', '_', key)
    return key

with open("enhanced_beat_stories.json") as f:
    data = json.load(f)

cleaned = []
for story in data:
    new_story = {}
    for k, v in story.items():
        if k.startswith("metadata_"):
            base = k[len("metadata_"):]
            new_key = "metadata_" + clean_key(base)
            new_story[new_key] = v
        else:
            new_story[k] = v
    cleaned.append(new_story)

with open("enhanced_beat_stories.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(cleaned, f, indent=2)
print("Cleaned metadata field names.")
```

3. After running the script, retry your import:
   ```bash
   rm -f beat_stories.db
   uv run sqlite-utils insert beat_stories.db stories enhanced_beat_stories.json --pk link
   uv run datasette beat_stories.db
   ```

BrendanWeissel: how to make a json file?

GitHub Copilot: To make a JSON file:

1. Open a text editor (like VS Code).
2. Write your data in valid JSON format. For example:

```json
[
  {
    "link": "https://example.com/story1",
    "title": "Story Title 1",
    "topic": "Sports",
    "tags": ["Tag1", "Tag2"],
    "summary": "This is a summary.",
    "content": "Full story content here."
  },
  {
    "link": "https://example.com/story2",
    "title": "Story Title 2",
    "topic": "News",
    "tags": ["TagA", "TagB"],
    "summary": "Another summary.",
    "content": "Another story content."
  }
]
```

3. Save the file with a `.json` extension, for example: `my_stories.json`.

**Tips:**
- JSON must use double quotes for keys and string values.
- Arrays are in `[ ... ]`, objects in `{ ... }`.
- You can use VS Code's "Format Document" feature for pretty formatting.
- To check if your file is valid JSON, you can use an online validator like https://jsonlint.com/.

Let me know if you want a template or want to create a file from scratch in your workspace!

GitHub Copilot: Two separate problems are shown in that error output — I'll explain each briefly and give concrete fixes/commands you can run.

1) cat: prompt.txt: No such file or directory
- Meaning: your shell tried to concatenate `prompt.txt` first, but that file doesn't exist in the current directory. The pipe still sent the JSON to the LLM, but missing the prompt file is probably not what you intended.
- Fix: create `prompt.txt` (the plain-text prompt you want to give the LLM), or remove it from the pipeline if you don't need it.

Example — create a simple prompt file:
```bash
# create prompt.txt with the instructions for the model
cat > prompt.txt <<'PROMPT'
Write a concise reporter's guide for covering this beat. Use the JSON that follows (stories.json) to:
- extract the top themes (3-5)
- list 5 key people and 5 key institutions
- suggest 8 story ideas with short ledes
Return Markdown only.
PROMPT
```

2) Error code 400 — prompt is too long: 202555 tokens > 200000 maximum
- Meaning: when you piped `prompt.txt` + enhanced_beat_stories.json into the LLM, the combined input exceeded the model/service token limit (200,000 tokens). The LLM API rejected the request.
- Fix: reduce the amount of input you send to the LLM. Typical approaches:
  - Send a much smaller JSON (a subset of stories).
  - Send a trimmed JSON with only the fields the model needs (title, summary, and a few metadata fields).
  - Chunk the JSON into batches and call the model repeatedly (generate partial outputs and then summarize/merge).
  - Summarize the JSON automatically before sending (e.g., precompute condensed summaries).

Concrete commands you can run (pick one):

A — Send a small subset of stories (fast, easy)
```bash
# take the first 50 stories (adjust the slice as needed)
jq '.[0:50]' enhanced_beat_stories.json > subset.json

# then run with your prompt + subset
cat prompt.txt subset.json | uv run llm -m claude-3.5-haiku > prototype.md
```

B — Reduce each story to only essential fields (title, summary, link, people, geographic focus)
```bash
jq '[.[] | {title, summary, link, metadata_people, metadata_geographic_focus}]' enhanced_beat_stories.json > small.json
cat prompt.txt small.json | uv run llm -m claude-3.5-haiku > prototype.md
```

C — Process in batches and merge results (recommended for very large files)
```bash
# create NDJSON (one JSON object per line)
jq -c '.[]' enhanced_beat_stories.json > stories.ndjson

# process in chunks of 50 and save outputs in a folder
mkdir -p llm_outputs
split -l 50 stories.ndjson llm_chunk_

for f in llm_chunk_*; do
  # rewrap chunk into an array for the model
  jq -s '.' $f > chunk.json
  cat prompt.txt chunk.json | uv run llm -m claude-3.5-haiku > llm_outputs/${f}.md
done

# later: combine/concatenate / post-process llm_outputs/*.md into prototype.md
cat llm_outputs/*.md > prototype.md
```

D — If you want a more compact single request, programmatically create a short meta-summary of the JSON first (e.g., extract counts, unique tags, most common people), then send only that summary to the LLM. I can show that command if you'd like.

Quick options (pick one). Each has copy/paste-ready commands you can run from your cns_collections directory.

1) Fast / low-effort — send a small subset
- Good when you only need a prototype or a quick result.

```bash
# take the first 50 stories

# create a prompt if you don't have one
cat > prompt.txt <<'PROMPT'

# run the LLM on the smaller file

```

2) Small payload — keep only fields the model needs
- Keeps more stories but dramatically reduces tokens by removing long `content`.

```bash
# keep only title, summary, link and key metadata fields
jq '[.[] | {title, summary, link, metadata_people, metadata_geographic_focus, metadata_story_type}]' enhanced_beat_stories.json > small.json

cat prompt.txt small.json | uv run llm -m claude-3.5-haiku > prototype.md
```

3) Full-data but safe — process in batches and merge results
- Best for full-dataset analysis without hitting token limits. Process N stories per request, collect outputs, then combine/aggregate.

```bash
# make ndjson, split into chunks of 50 lines (change 50 as needed)
jq -c '.[]' enhanced_beat_stories.json > stories.ndjson
split -l 50 stories.ndjson chunk_

mkdir -p llm_outputs
for f in chunk_*; do
  jq -s '.' "$f" > chunk.json
  cat prompt.txt chunk.json | uv run llm -m claude-3.5-haiku > llm_outputs/$f.md
  rm chunk.json
done

# combine outputs (you may want to post-process instead of raw cat)
cat llm_outputs/*.md > prototype.md
```

4) Pre-summarize programmatically, then ask the LLM to synthesize
- Create a compact summary (top tags, counts, sample summaries) and send that smaller summary to the model.

Example: extract top tags, most common people and story counts
```bash
# top 50 tags (compact)
jq -r '.[] | .tags[]?' enhanced_beat_stories.json | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -n 50 > top_tags.txt

# top people from metadata (if present)
jq -r '.[] | (.metadata_people // "[]") | fromjson?[]?' enhanced_beat_stories.json 2>/dev/null \
  | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -n 50 > top_people.txt

# small summary file
{
  echo "Top tags:"; cat top_tags.txt
  echo; echo "Top people:"; cat top_people.txt
  echo; echo "Sample story titles and summaries:"; jq -r '.[] | "\nTitle: \(.title)\nSummary: \(.summary)\n"' enhanced_beat_stories.json | head -n 200
} > compact_summary.txt

# send compact_summary.txt to the model
cat prompt.txt compact_summary.txt | uv run llm -m claude-3.5-haiku > prototype.md
```

Notes and tips
- Creating `prompt.txt` matters: include clear instructions and ask the model to ignore raw JSON fields you don't need.
- Removing long `content` fields is the biggest token-saver. Summaries + titles are usually enough for a beat guide.
- If you want a single final output from many batches, run a final pass that asks the model to merge batch outputs (or write a small script to aggregate).

# SCRIPT CREATION 

I worked back and forth with CoPilot to create the script. At first it was confused about the list it needed to make me for topics options. So once it gave me a draft of topics I let it run for about 20 stories and then modified it. At first the list did not take the star dem into account and gave a generic list, then the list was too long. Finally I got one I am happier with and let it run for the 200 stories. 



### Results Analysis

Here is the breakdown of topics and how many stories in them: 
events 31
arts 28
government 27
sports 27
safety 18
education 10
business 9
health 9
other 8
agriculture 6
development 6
environment 6
obituary 6
planning 5
housing 3
fisheries 1

The topics work. I should have flagged the "other" category however I don't think it is necessarily bad to have. As we saw the Star-Democrat sometimes does things like "this day in history" so that type of stuff may be classified as that. A few of the stories in "other" from my set of stories are from relgious figures. 

The top categories is what I would expect for a local news organization like the star democrat. A lot of focus on community events and arts. With a focus on gov and sports. The art category is a bit all over the place with church stories, celebrity updates and cooking stories. If I was to do this again I may try and split up these stories. I think a religion category may be useful. 

 The LLM did a good job with a few modifications. I had to have it get narrowed down but for overall stories with a slight focus on the star democrat it got the job done. One of the niche categories it selected was "fisheries" but then only 1 story was classified as that. Those stories seemed to get grouped into other categories like environemnt as well. As I mentioned arts is a bit too broad the rest I am happy with the results. The main mis-categorization is in the arts section. It would need to be split up in future models. I also think "events" is a weird category because some of the stories are future events and some are event recaps. That should be clarified in the future. 

If I was to do this again I would open up the category list a bit more to clarify arts, events and other. I like the government tag but it may be better to divide that up as well for tiers of government. 

Using Approach 1 and having the LLM is my prefered method because of how it can look at all the stories before deciding the categories. Also I did give a bit of my input to revise the list so I did not run all 200 stories until I was happy with the results.

After doing this assignment I feel more confident using CoPolit and Github to get a list of topics and think if I did this again it would be much faster. With more time refining this list and process will lead us to a solid foundation of topics.
